archetypes.name: token-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan's hardest stated failure mode is a half-applied --approve rename; verify the scope-file list is exhaustive and the rg guard correctly partitions public vs internal tokens across the full repo.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether the scope-file list covers every file that embeds the public --approve flag token in machine-readable positions (argument-hint strings, completion stubs, plugin.json, other docs/ files, other skills/ siblings) by looking for --approve occurrences outside the stated scope. Verify the plan's rg negative-lookahead guard ((?<![A-Za-z0-9_])--approve(?!-requested)) correctly covers all internal-token forms without false positives on --approve-requested, approve_requested, and APPROVE_REQUESTED, and without false negatives from variants like --approve= or --approve followed by a tab or newline. Verify that the stated allowlist of intentional residue (retired-flag parser test, flags.md retirement note, CHANGELOG history) is complete and that no additional machine-readable positions need covering. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: count-drift
archetypes.rationale: Adding one KV bumps the expected-count literal from 8 to 9 across at least four distinct locations; verify the plan addresses every location and none is left at the stale value.
archetypes.prompt_body: Identify every location in the scope files where the parser output count appears as a literal: the _success_kv_count -ne check in SKILL.md Step 0-pre, the 'exactly these eight KVs' and exit-code table wording in parse-design-argv.md, the assert_success_kv_count calls in test-parse-design-argv.sh, and any structural-test pins in test-design-structure.sh that grep for the count literal. Verify the plan explicitly addresses each of these locations and changes the value from 8 to 9 in its per-file change descriptions; note any location present in the source files but absent from the plan. Also check whether design-init-runparams.md or write-run-params.md carry a KV-count statement that would need updating. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: gate-wire
archetypes.rationale: The two auto-approve gates have different mechanics (1d.7 writes .outline-approved; Gate C writes no sentinel); verify the plan's sentinel, breadcrumb, and AskUserQuestion suppression descriptions are internally consistent and leave no silent path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the plan's auto-approve description for Step 1d.7 (write .outline-approved sentinel on auto-approve, print breadcrumb, no AskUserQuestion) against the Gate C description (no new sentinel, suppress existing AskUserQuestion, proceed to Step 5) and verify the differences are intentional and fully accounted for in the plan's prose for design-outline.md and approval-gates.md respectively. Check whether the AskUserQuestion suppression at Gate C covers all option paths the existing gate exposes — including Discuss-further, round-cap re-run, and any cap-aware option text — so none can fire when skip_approve_requested=true. Verify that the SKILL.md Step 1d.7 section's statement that the new fence 'writes no completion sentinel' is consistent with what the plan says design-outline.md will do, which does write .outline-approved. Confirm the plan's two breadcrumb strings are unique and stable enough for test-design-structure.sh grep pins without colliding with any existing breadcrumb in the repo. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
